checks: Twelve live MCP tools with machine-readable schemas; both adapters run without arguments
Passive connection report distinguishes missing broker, live MCP hosts and exact window registration
PuTTY-first startup, C output and incremental reading through two MCP connections
Native fixture accepts only exact device command bytes and Enter; task output and transcript contain no injected wrapper
One approval shows configured source and target; pending approval outlives the one-second execution budget; no second client can replace it
Native Ctrl+C sequence correlates prompt return without inventing an exit code
Reject, cancel, and manual input invalidate the exact pending command; repeated request ID cannot reopen it

A literal expected_prompt tracks the changed device mode without sending extra input
Foreground H3C fixture receives one Space, Enter and Ctrl+C under separate approvals, guards stale rendered frames and returns its original prompt
Attach and detach are owner-bound, typed Unicode and multiline paste are individually approved, and human takeover revokes pending input
Standalone SSH exit status is accepted before channel close and blocks new keys
Dedicated top protocol separates rendered frames, key dispatch, channel closure, exit status and exit signal
Top ownership is enforced; a channel closing during approval revokes the pending key
Vi startup and quit have separate local approvals; named keys are allowlisted, one-shot per request and tied to the active owned PTY
Vi text approval shows exact multiline Unicode and source; invalid input and cross-profile use are rejected; duplicate requests send once; explicit discard has its own prompt
Vi file open and save show the exact approved path; invalid paths, scratch saves, foreign clients, rejection, replay and closed tasks are enforced
Automatic mode isolates foreground input between child windows and runs supported commands, vi actions, interrupt and child lifecycle without dialogs
native ring overflow discloses missing bytes without waiting for MCP
broker killed: native GUI heartbeat survives; native and MCP reconnect without remote reconnection
MCP adapter crash does not interrupt another reader or native output
Disable closes IPC and rejects the old identity; enabling after MCP starts registers a fresh session
